issue: Does a prior conviction qualify as a 'controlled substance offense' under U.S.S.G. § 4B1.2(b) only if the substance is listed in the federal Controlled Substances Act, or may the term be defined by reference to state law?

sides.position: A 'controlled substance offense' under § 4B1.2(b) requires that the offense involve a substance listed in the federal Controlled Substances Act; the term is defined by federal law.
cases: United States v. Townsend, 897 F.3d 66 (2d Cir. 2018)
United States v. Bautista, 989 F.3d 698 (9th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Crocco, 15 F.4th 20 (1st Cir. 2021)
United States v. Gomez-Alvarez, 781 F.3d 787 (5th Cir. 2015)

sides.position: The term 'controlled substance' in § 4B1.2(b) is defined by reference to state law as well as federal law, so an offense involving a substance controlled under state law can qualify.
cases: United States v. Ward, 972 F.3d 364 (4th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Ramirez, 52 F.4th 705 (7th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Henderson, 11 F.4th 713 (8th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Jones, 15 F.4th 1288 (10th Cir. 2021)

this_court: The Seventh Circuit adheres to the state-law approach from United States v. Ruth and declines to overrule it, so a state-law controlled substance can qualify under § 4B1.2(b).
quote: In contrast, the Fourth[,] … Seventh, Eighth, and Tenth Circuits[] define[] what qualifies as a “controlled substance” based on the relevant state law.
cite: United States v. Christopher Ramirez, 52 F.4th 705 (7th Cir. 2022)
